Public Portion 
 1. Multifamily development projects in the city of Springfield and what possible 
amendment(s) exist to the City's Zoning Regulations regarding the Tier 3—City 
Council Special Permit review thresholds. 
 2. Ordinance amendment relating to the City's Historic Districts under Chapter 49 and 
Historic Preservation under Chapter 218. 
On October 26, 2026, the Planning and Economic Development Committee, chaired by 
Councilor Jose Delgado, met to review proposed amendments to multifamily housing special 
permit requirements and the City's Historic Preservation Ordinance. Chief Development Officer 
Tim Sheehan and Planning Department representatives presented a proposed zoning overlay 
limited to the Court Square Urban Renewal Plan area, increasing the City Council special permit 
threshold from 10 to 50 dwelling units for new construction and from 26 to 65 units for adaptive 
reuse projects. Existing requirements outside the proposed overlay would remain unchanged. 
Discussion addressed downtown housing development, regulatory barriers, the Council's 
oversight authority, Planning Board review, and neighborhood participation. Councilor Kateri 
Walsh expressed concerns about reducing Council oversight, while other members discussed 
balancing development opportunities with neighborhood protections. Planning officials agreed to 
develop language requiring neighborhood council engagement and return to the committee for 
further review. 
 
The committee also reviewed proposed revisions consolidating the City's historic district and 
demolition delay ordinances, including updated definitions, enforcement provisions, historic
district designation procedures, and application requirements. Representatives of the Community 
Preservation Committee and Springfield Preservation Trust raised concerns regarding additional 
requirements for single-building historic districts, proposed application fees, eligibility standards 
for historic designation, and the omission of municipal project review procedures. Bob 
McCarroll requested removal or modification of Article 3, Section C, to protect Community 
Preservation Act-funded properties, while the Preservation Trust recommended further 
consideration of historic designation criteria, fees, and notification procedures. Discussion 
included the proposed $1,000 historic district application fee and the existing 75-year demolition 
review threshold. 
 
Councilor Delgado requested additional review of both proposals before advancing either item to 
the full City Council. Planning officials agreed to provide revised neighborhood engagement 
language, additional information regarding historic district fees in comparable communities, and 
a summary identifying substantive changes to the historic preservation ordinance. Both matters 
remained under committee review, with a follow-up meeting to be scheduled. No formal 
recommendation or substantive vote was recorded. The meeting concluded at 6:27 p.m.
